analysis: What changed since the 4:00 AM PT brief: the morning got its first real earnings print, and it cut both ways. Verizon's Q3 (reported ~4:21 AM PT) beat on adjusted EPS ($1.31 vs ~$1.27 expected) and nearly doubled subscriber-add expectations (406,000 vs ~209,000), raised full-year guidance, and added a >$2B AWS AI-fiber deal — but revenue ($34.313B) missed the ~$34.74B estimate, and shares still rose 2.4% premarket, so the market is rewarding the subscriber/guidance story over the revenue miss. The second change is in the neocloud story: it is no longer just Musk's warning. Nebius's own CEO now concedes asset-backed and debt financing have 'temporarily dried up,' even as Nebius points to a $3.5B Citi facility secured Thursday and says it has enough to build its gigawatt — a company confirming the funding squeeze while insisting it is funded. Premarket megacaps split in a way that fits that framing: Tesla +2.28% and Nvidia +1.03% held up while Apple slipped 1.52% premarket (Finnhub 07:57 ET read), a reminder the 4 AM 'Apple tops Nvidia' rotation is not a one-way street. Futures still point to a calmer open (Reuters 05:19 ET: Dow +0.49%, S&P +0.30%, Nasdaq +0.25%) on the oil pullback, but the Qatar mediation track is unproven — Houthi attacks continued over the weekend and Mecca Pact officials only meet Tehran today. Signal vs noise: Verizon's print, the oil pullback, the Nebius CEO comments and the Wednesday earnings/Fed calendar are confirmed; the SpaceX $40B pricing detail remains single-source/unconfirmed; the eOption futures table showing a smaller bounce was not used because its Brent quote conflicted with Reuters-sourced prints. USAC's catalyst today is mechanical (record/ex-dividend date), not fundamental.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: US stock futures pointed higher Monday into the open: at 05:19 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis +257 points (+0.49%), S&P 500 E-minis +23.25 points (+0.30%), Nasdaq 100 E-minis +73 points (+0.25%) (Reuters), after the S&P 500 logged losses for the last two weeks.
headlines.why_it_matters: A modest relief bounce on easing oil sets a calmer open — but it is relief, not conviction, with the Fed decision and two hyperscaler prints landing Wednesday.

headlines.headline: Verizon (VZ) reported Q3 before the open: adjusted EPS $1.31 (vs ~$1.27 consensus), revenue $34.313B (+1.5% y/y, vs ~$34.74B expected — a miss), postpaid phone adds 406,000 (vs ~209,000 expected). Verizon raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $5.04-$5.06 (from $4.99-$5.04) and subscriber-add guidance to 1.1-1.2M, and signed a >$2B AI infrastructure deal with AWS for fiber connectivity to AWS data centers. Shares rose 2.4% premarket (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: Subscriber beats plus raised guidance outweighed a revenue miss — and the AWS fiber deal ties a telecom name directly into the AI-infrastructure spend the market is repricing.

headlines.headline: Oil kept pulling back Monday: WTI $101.04 (-2.16%) and Brent $114.51 (-1.89%) at 0426 GMT, after Friday settlements of $103.27 and $116.72. Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran on Sunday in coordination with the US, and top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are due to meet Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday — but Houthi attacks on Saudi pipeline pumping stations and Riyadh airport continued over the weekend, and Saudi Arabia said it intercepted more missiles and drones (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: Mediation headlines are trimming the war premium, but with attacks still happening the ~2% pullback is a dent in the premium, not its removal.

headlines.headline: Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh conceded neocloud financing has tightened — asset-backed financing and debt markets have 'temporarily dried up' — while saying Nebius has enough funding to build its planned gigawatt, via customer advances and other instruments. Nebius secured a $3.5B debt facility from Citi on Thursday for data-center expansion and GPU purchases. NBIS is down ~33% this month (Stocktwits/TradingView).
headlines.why_it_matters: The funding squeeze is now confirmed by a neocloud CEO, not just Musk — it keeps the megacap/neocloud split as the tape's main fault line into Wednesday's hyperscaler prints.

headlines.headline: Premarket megacaps split at the 07:57 ET Finnhub read: Tesla +2.28%, Nvidia +1.03%, Microsoft +0.44%, while Apple slipped 1.52% premarket — after Apple briefly topped Nvidia as the world's most valuable company on Oct 23 (single-source TIKR print in the 4 AM brief).
headlines.why_it_matters: Tesla and Nvidia holding up while Apple fades premarket shows the rotation inside tech is two-way — dip-buying is selective, not broad, ahead of Wednesday.

headlines.headline: Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday after the close, hours after the 2:00 p.m. ET Fed decision (Alphabet call 4:30 p.m. ET, Microsoft 5:30 p.m. ET). Consensus: Microsoft ~$90.6B revenue / $4.71 adjusted EPS with Azure growth guided at 45% constant-currency and quarterly capex above $50B; Alphabet ~$127.9B revenue / $3.00 EPS after Google Cloud grew 82% last quarter. Amazon reports Thursday after the close (consensus ~$202.2B revenue / $1.96 EPS).
headlines.why_it_matters: Wednesday stacks the Fed decision and two hyperscaler prints into one afternoon — cloud growth vs capex vs cash flow is the exact test the market has been demanding since Meta's selloff.

headlines.headline: Meta earnings context carried forward: Meta beat on revenue and raised Q4 guidance last week yet shares fell 7% Thursday and another 1% Friday, as higher AI spending turned free cash flow negative and its five-year CDS spread hit a record (The Daily Upside). CoreWeave's five-year CDS implied a >50% chance of default over five years, and Gartner predicts 80% of neocloud providers could cease independent operations by 2030.
headlines.why_it_matters: Meta is the cautionary template for Wednesday: even a revenue beat sells off when AI spend swamps cash flow — that is the bar MSFT and GOOGL now face.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. Today is mechanical: Monday Oct 26 is both the record date and ex-dividend date for the Q3 cash distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield), payable Nov 6. Q3 earnings arrive before the open Tue Nov 3 with an 11 a.m. ET call. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. Carried context: on Oct 1 USAC issued 34,467,347 new Class A units (9.25% fixed annual distribution, non-convertible, non-redeemable) to subsidiary J-W Energy in an internal reorganization. With WTI pulling back to ~$101 but still near six-month highs, the energy backdrop for compression demand stays supportive with no company-specific catalyst.
